entry.title: How are you handling the reconciliation of opening subcontracting stock under Indian GST in SAP?
entry.content:
I’m curious to know what is Standard or Best approach Opening Subcontracting Stock Reconciliation using transaction J1IGRECON.

The Scenario:

Imagine you have migrated opening subcontracting stock (e.g., 100,000 kg of raw material) sent out to vendor locations across multiple, different historical subcontracting challans:

  • Migration: Stock is uploaded using movement type 561 O (Opening balance for stock provided to vendor).

  • Goods Receipt: The finished goods/processed materials are subsequently received back via movement type 101 (with 543 O for raw material consumption).

The Technical Dilemma:

Since the stock was initialized via 561 O without a direct reference to original pre-migration 180-day GST tracking challans in the system:

  1. How do you map and reconcile the 101 Goods Receipts against the uploaded opening challans in J1IGRECON?

  2. How are you handling line-item level matching when bulk quantity (100,000 kg) is distributed across dozens of legacy challans?

  3. What best practices or custom workarounds have worked best for you to prevent GST compliance issues (like 180-day ITC reversal/tax liability risks)?

entry.title: SAP EWM auto WT failed due to no empty bin found after the UD in QA32.
entry.content:
Hi Experts

I am working on SAP S/4HANA Embedded EWM 2022 integrated with ERP Quality Management

I am facing an issue after the Usage Decision process for rejected stock

The inspection is completed in QA32 and the Usage Decision is successfully posted. After the Usage Decision the system creates an automatic Warehouse Task to move the stock to the rejected storage type

The problem started because the rejected storage type became completely full. As a result, the automatic Warehouse Task could not move the stock to the destination bin.

To continue warehouse operations, the warehouse user manually moved the rejected stock to another available storage bin.

After the manual movement, the stock type changed correctly according to the Usage Decision. The stock is also updated correctly in ERP and the warehouse process is completed successfully.

However, in EWM Monitor, the stock still shows the Inspection Lot reference even though the Usage Decision has already been completed and the stock is no longer under quality inspection.

There is also a stuck qRFC queue in SMQ2 with the error message "Error during follow-up action. See application log." The queue cannot be processed successfully.

I would like to understand why the Inspection Lot reference is still attached to the stock after the Usage Decision has been completed.

Could the failed Warehouse Task caused by the full rejected storage type have interrupted the QM follow-up action?

Is the stuck qRFC queue responsible for keeping the Inspection Lot reference active?

Which application log or transaction should I check to identify the root cause of this issue?

Has anyone experienced a similar issue in SAP S/4HANA Embedded EWM with ERP QM integration?

Any suggestions, troubleshooting steps, or relevant SAP Notes would be greatly appreciated.

Thank you.

entry.title: Road Freight Accrual Issue in Ocean Freight - SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition
entry.content:
Hi everyone,

I am testing an Ocean Freight scenario in the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition Starter System using the following scopes:

  • 6W2 – Manual Transportation Planning
  • 6W3 – Transportation Execution
  • 6W4 – Freight Settlement

As part of the Ocean Freight process, the transportation consists of:

Road Pre-Carriage → Ocean Main Carriage → Road On-Carriage

The Road Freight Orders for the pre-carriage and on-carriage are automatically created as part of the Ocean Freight Booking process.

The Ocean Freight Booking itself is working successfully. I am able to:

  • Calculate the ocean freight charges
  • Perform accrual posting
  • Create the Service PO and SES
  • Post the freight supplier invoice

However, I am unable to perform accrual posting for the Road Freight Orders created from the Ocean Freight Booking.

For the Road Freight Orders:

  • The Road Freight Orders are created successfully.
  • The respective road carriers are maintained in the Freight Agreement.
  • The required truck/equipment has been assigned.
  • However, charges are not being calculated for the Road Freight Orders.
  • The Road Freight Orders do not appear in Monitor Accrual Postings – Freight Documents.
  • Attempting to process the invoice directly also does not work.

My understanding is that the Road Freight Orders should have their own applicable freight charges and should subsequently become available for accrual posting and settlement.

Could someone clarify what is preventing the Road Freight Orders created from an Ocean Freight Booking from being charge-calculated and appearing in Monitor Accrual Postings in the Starter System?

Specifically:

  1. Are there any additional prerequisites for charge calculation on these Road Freight Orders?
  2. Does the Road Freight Order require a specific execution/posting status before it becomes available for accrual posting?
  3. Should the Freight Agreement/Calculation Sheet/Rate Table be maintained specifically for the Road Freight Orders, even though they were created from the Ocean Freight Booking?
  4. Is there any specific configuration required for the pre-carriage and on-carriage road legs in an Ocean Freight scenario?

Any guidance on the expected standard behavior and troubleshooting steps for 6W2/6W3/6W4 Ocean Freight in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition would be appreciated.

entry.title: Converting PR to PO - Currency Inconsistency Error After SAP S/4HANA 2025 Upgrade from SAP S/4HANA
entry.content:
We recently upgraded our system from SAP S/4HANA 2021 to SAP S/4HANA 2025. Since the upgrade, we have encountered an issue when converting Purchase Requisitions (PRs) to Purchase Orders (POs).

Scenario:

  • Purchase Requisition is created in NZD
  • Supplier's purchasing currency is AUD
  • Purchasing Info Record is maintained in AUD
  • During PO creation/conversion from the PR, the system issues the error:

"Inconsistent currency information"

Prior to the upgrade, the same process worked without any issues, and SAP automatically allowed the conversion despite the currency difference between the PR and the Info Record.

Questions:

  1. Has there been any change in standard SAP S/4HANA 2025 currency validation logic for Purchase Requisition to Purchase Order conversion?
  2. Are there any new configuration settings, business functions, or SAP Notes that enforce stricter currency consistency checks in S/4HANA 2025?
  3. Is this expected standard behavior after the upgrade, or could it indicate a missing configuration or post-upgrade correction?
  4. Are there any recommended settings to allow PRs in NZD to be converted into POs using an AUD Purchasing Info Record, as was possible in S/4HANA 2021?

Any guidance on the changes introduced in S/4HANA 2025 that may have impacted this process would be appreciated.

entry.title: Query_SAP MM
entry.content:
SAP MM Query: Wanted to have Pull-in exceptions with MRP type VB — anyone solved this?

Working through an MRP scenario and would like the community's input.
We're using MRP type VB (reorder point planning) for a set of materials, but pull-in exception messages aren't triggering.

Ex : ROP is 10, Stock is 0.
PR generated and PO converted with the delivery date of 12months from Today, but there is no pull in exception.
So it was unaddressed and led to a risk.

Options explored :
VB + Safety stock ---> No exceptions
V1 Type : No exceptions.
PD Type : Not feasible.

Turns out this isn't a bug: VB doesn't do date-based requirements netting, so pull-in logic simply doesn't apply to it. That's reserved for MRP types like PD.

Curious how others have handled this:
Have you used time-phased planning (R1/R2)? If yes, please explain.

Would appreciate hearing how other SAP MM folks have approached this trade-off between planning simplicity and requirement responsiveness.

@SAP
#SAPMM #S4HANA #MaterialsManagement #SupplyChain
